PullRequest.Title: ripple: drop the 50% limit and always run only the affected unit tests
PullRequest.Body:

Follow-up to #342907.

## What

`ripple plan` had a cost-based cutoff: when the selected unit tests were more than `--max-share` (default 0.5) of the unit test work, it reported `running every unit test: the change affects N% of the unit test work (limit 50%)` and set `select: false`, so macOS and Windows ran every unit test. This removes it, without a replacement threshold. A plan now either selects exactly the unit test files that a change can affect, however many, or runs every unit test for a dependency reason only (`Selection::run_all`): a `runEverything` file, a package or script of the test runners, a module that the runners use, or a module that does not parse. Linux still runs every unit test on every push.

- `build/ripple/src/main.rs`: `--max-share` is gone from the usage, the option list and the parsing (passing it now fails with `unknown option '--max-share'`), and so are the `max_share` parameter of `plan()` and its reason. `select` is `sel.run_all.is_none()`. `share` stays in `plan.json` and in the reason of a selection, as information. rustfmt now packs `OPTIONS` onto two lines: `"max-share"` was its only element longer than rustfmt's threshold for short array elements (10 characters).
- `build/ripple/README.md`: the CI paragraph and the `plan` command no longer mention the limit.

`pr.yml` never passed `--max-share` and needs no change: its `Check ripple` step reads `.reason` only for `parse error (`, and `.select` and `.unit` for a plan that selects nothing.

### What the limit cost

On the replay of the 708 first-parent commits of `main` from Oct 13 to 20 (the one in the README), 18 commits (2.5%) went over the limit. They would have selected 69.6% of the unit test work on average, and ran all of it. Without the limit, the macOS and Windows unit test work per commit drops from 9.8% to 9.0% of a full run on average, about 0.4 VM minutes per push: the unit test steps of a full run took 49.4 VM minutes on macOS and Windows in [the last run of #344104](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/40176001254), which ran every unit test.

### Open pull requests that read `plan.json`

Neither depends on the limit's reason text:

- #344108 (`ripple/skip-browser-jobs`) reads `.reason` only for `parse error (`, and `.select` and `.unit`. It rewrites the same README sentence and keeps "or when it affects more than half of the unit test work", so whichever of the two merges second has a one-line conflict there: drop that clause.
- #344106 (`ripple/recall-warning`) reads `.select` and `unit.txt`. The plans that went over the limit now select, so its recall check covers them too.

## Validation

- `cd build/ripple && cargo +nightly-2026-04-14 fmt && cargo test --release --locked && cargo build --release --locked`: passed. rustfmt's only change is the `OPTIONS` layout above; 72 tests passed; the release build has no warnings.
- **The 18 commits that went over the limit now select.** For each commit of the replay with `decl > 0.5` and `runAll == null`: `ripple plan --config build/ripple/vscode.jsonc --base <sha>^1 --head <sha>`, with this branch's binary and with the one built from a383e086268 (#342907), which has the limit. This branch selects in all 18, exactly the replay's `declTestFiles`, and both binaries list identical files (`.unit`). The replay predates #344104, but #344104 changes none of these selections: its own replay found all 708 commits identical on `declTestFiles` and `runAll`. The shares match up to the rounding of `share` to 4 decimals in `plan.json` (largest difference 0.00005).

- **The 16 commits that run everything still do:** `select: false`, with the replay's `runAll` reason (12 test job definitions, 2 test runners, 1 transpiler, 1 runtime version).
- **The CI path**, for the commit of #334259 (83.9%), with `--out-dir`, `GITHUB_OUTPUT` and `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`: `select=true`, a `unit.txt` with 1,820 files, and a job summary that lists them. The `Check ripple` expressions of `pr.yml` on that `plan.json`: no parse warning, `selects-nothing=false`.
- `ripple plan --config vscode.jsonc --base HEAD --max-share 0.5`: `Error: unknown option '--max-share'`.
- `git grep -nE 'max-share|max_share|half of the unit test|limit 50|\(limit ' -- build/ripple .github test/unit build/lib`: no matches.
- `node --experimental-strip-types build/hygiene.ts build/ripple/src/main.rs build/ripple/README.md`: passed (it checks `main.rs`; `README.md` is not eligible). The pre-commit hook passed too.
- Not run locally: the workflows. Since this changes `build/ripple`, its CI runs every unit test, and the `Ripple` check builds, tests and plans with this branch.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: The default 50% cutoff discarded an already-computed affected-test selection and eagerly executed every unit test on macOS and Windows, adding unaffected test files in proportion to the gap between the selected share and 100%.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: PRs whose affected-test weight exceeded 50% consumed unnecessary macOS/Windows CI VM time and had longer unit-test critical paths; the replay indicates an average selected share of 69.6% for triggering commits and about 0.4 VM-minute average savings per push after removing the cutoff.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: For graph-contained changes, the plan now always emits and uploads the selected unit-test list regardless of weighted share. Each unchanged test runner filters its discovered modules through that list, avoiding execution of the unaffected 0-50% rather than expanding every selection above 50% to a full run.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: The base-revision condition at line 373 turns selection off whenever the already-computed weighted share exceeds max_share (default 0.5). In PR CI, `select: false` prevents upload of `unit.txt`; the four macOS/Windows unit jobs then invoke their Electron, Node, or browser runners without `--runList`, and each runner loads its full default module set. The changed RIGHT line 365 now bases selection only on `sel.run_all`, preserving the computed file list for changes above 50%. The PR's replay supplies concrete observed scale: 18/708 commits crossed the cutoff, averaging 69.6% selected work but previously executing 100%, while the full macOS/Windows unit steps consumed 49.4 VM-minutes.

Scenarios.Scenario: Detect Changes generates a Ripple plan for a PR merge commit whose affected unit-test share is above the former 50% cutoff.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The Ripple binary must finish repository snapshotting, graph construction, selection, JSON/list generation, and local plan writes before the artifact can be uploaded and macOS/Windows unit jobs can consume it. The changed decision does not add graph analysis: `selected` and `share` were already computed before the old cutoff.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run Git CLI operations for repository root resolution, two tree snapshots, batched blob reads, and the base/head tree diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: A fixed set of tree/diff Git commands per plan plus blob reads batched through one `git cat-file --batch` process per existing analysis worker; cardinality is independent of whether the selected share is above 50%.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same snapshots, graph analysis, affected-file selection, and share calculation ran before the cutoff was evaluated.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These operations dominate plan construction and must finish before output generation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Write plan.json, unit.txt, GITHUB_OUTPUT, and a job-summary entry for each selected file.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: For an above-cutoff graph-contained change, one plan file, one list file containing the effective selected set, two small append targets, and one summary line per selected file; observed replay selections range from 1,083 to 1,828 files.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: plan.json was still written, but select=false suppressed unit.txt and per-file summary lines for shares above max_share.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Small local serialization/writes occur after selection and before the plan step completes; cost scales linearly with selected paths but remains bounded by the repository's unit-test file count.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Upload the generated unit-test-plan workflow artifact.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One small artifact per successful selecting plan, containing plan.json and unit.txt; newly occurs for graph-contained selections above 50%.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Above-cutoff plans set select=false, so no artifact was uploaded.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Upload gates availability to downstream unit jobs, but payload grows only with test-path text and is tiny relative to checkout/build/test execution.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Repository module count controls unchanged graph analysis; the effective selected unit-test file count controls only added path serialization. Historical triggering commits selected 1,083-1,828 files (59.6%-83.9% weighted share), bounded by the full unit-test set.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Snapshot analysis uses the existing Rayon worker pool and batched `git cat-file` readers; the plan command itself is one workflow step. Artifact upload is one action after planning. The diff does not increase analysis or subprocess concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The Ripple executable's GitHub Actions cache is unchanged. Within a plan invocation, Engine content analysis remains cached by blob OID across base/head snapshots; there is no cross-run graph cache. A warm binary cache avoids build/test as before. Artifact retention and keys are unchanged; the changed path creates an artifact for above-50% selections.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed line 365 is reached after unchanged selection/share computation and directly changes output generation and artifact eligibility for above-cutoff plans.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact artifact and summary-write milliseconds are not measured, but their bounded path-text payload is clearly minor compared with the avoided unit-test execution. No actionable regression is established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The small new serialization/artifact work enables a measured reduction in downstream test work, and the PR fixes the old eager full-run behavior.

Scenarios.Scenario: macOS and Windows Electron, Node, and browser unit jobs consume an above-50% selected plan.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each of the four OS/suite jobs downloads the plan after Detect Changes, then the relevant test steps run sequentially within that job. Job completion remains gated by test execution, but runners now load only selected modules instead of all default modules.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Download the unit-test-plan artifact in each selected unit job.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One download attempt in each of four unit jobs. Before the diff these jobs still executed the download action with a pattern but found no artifact; after the diff they download one small plan artifact.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The download action was already on every selection-enabled unit job path; above the cutoff there was no matching artifact and runners fell back to all tests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The successful small download precedes tests, adding bounded network/file extraction work but enabling reduced test execution.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Launch Electron, Node, and browser unit-test runners, which discover the default files and optionally filter them through the run-list Set before loading test modules.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Six runner invocations across macOS and Windows (Electron and Node in each Electron job, one browser runner in each browser job), unchanged. Effective loaded module/test work changes from 100% to the selected weighted share, historically 59.6%-83.9% for cited triggering commits.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: For shares above 50%, select=false meant no run list, so the same six runners loaded their complete default module sets.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Test runner completion dominates each job. Filtering adds linear Set construction/membership checks over selected/discovered paths but avoids loading and executing all unaffected modules.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The affected test weight and selected file count after Ripple's declaration-level deduplication control test work. The replay shows 18/708 commits triggering the old cutoff, averaging 69.6% selected work; the changed path executes that effective set rather than 100%.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The four macOS/Windows unit jobs can run in parallel as before. Within each Electron unit job, Electron and Node test steps are sequential; each browser unit job has one browser runner. The diff changes module cardinality, not job or process concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The workflow artifact is produced once and downloaded per job; no changed test-result cache is involved. Cold or warm Ripple binary caches affect only planning and do not alter this decision. Runner file discovery remains unchanged, while the in-process run-list Set is rebuilt once per runner invocation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: workflow expressions pass `--runList` exactly when plan.json exists, and each runner filters discovered files before module loading. The changed select decision is the sole reason above-cutoff plans now reach that path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Per-commit timing varies by test weights and runner/platform overhead, but the PR provides a concrete 49.4 VM-minute full-run baseline and an aggregate estimate of about 0.4 VM-minute savings per push.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. This is a high-confidence eager-work performance fix: it preserves process cardinality and reduces loaded/executed tests, with only bounded list handling and artifact overhead.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed the complete two-file diff and traced plan generation through Git subprocesses, filesystem output, artifact transfer, and all macOS/Windows unit-runner consumers. No performance regression was introduced. Recorded the removal of the 50% full-run cutoff as a concrete eager-work regression fix attributed to a383e08626828ceb9c32f45f4a2940070a2f27f1.
